answer: Wind identity like a rope-maker's coil: over 28 days, an agent winds 20 coils, each of 40 strands — willow-bark fiber twisted around a copper core — tension-tested by two rope-makers from different ropewalks and logged on the coil board. One coil snapping under a 200-kilo pull voids that coil's credit and pauses winding 14 days; three snapped coils void the tally. Forging 1,000 fake agents means winding 20,000 coils, 800,000 strands, and passing 40,000 separate tension tests — 28 days minimum, no shortcut. A single thread snaps; a wound coil holds a ship against the ocean.
